messages.text: Djokovic to return to China Open on Sky Sports after 11-year absence

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic has confirmed he will compete at the China Open this year, which runs from September 30-October 6 live on Sky Sports, marking a return to the event following an 11-year absence.
metadata.content: Novak Djokovic to return to ATP's China Open on Sky Sports after 11-year absence from event | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Novak Djokovic to return to ATP's China Open on Sky Sports after 11-year absence from event Novak Djokovic announces he will return to ATP Tour's China Open for first time since 2015 between September 30-October 6, live on Sky Sports; Decision comes following shock US Open first-round exit; watch Laver Cup at O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports Wednesday 16 September 2026 19:37, UK Image: Novak Djokovic has announced he will return to the China Open for the first time in 11 years Novak Djokovic has confirmed he will compete at the China Open this year, which runs from September 30-October 6 live on Sky Sports , marking a return to the event following an 11-year absence. The 39-year-old recently dropped as low as No 12 in the world rankings following a shock first-round defeat to Argentina's Mariano Navone at the US Open. That defeat followed on from a third-round exit in May at the French Open - two underwhelming Grand Slam displays coming either side of a run to the semi-finals at Wimbledon, where he was well beaten in straight sets by eventual champion Jannik Sinner. Djokovic has not won a Grand Slam title since 2023, going three full calendar years without success. messages.text: 'It's my scar, not yours' - Tuchel defends World Cup semi-final subs

metadata.summary: Thomas Tuchel has passionately defended his controversial defensive substitutions during England's World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.
metadata.content: Thomas Tuchel: England head coach defends controversial World Cup semi-final substitutions with Argentina adding: 'It's my scar, not yours' | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Thomas Tuchel: England head coach defends controversial World Cup semi-final substitutions with Argentina adding: 'It's my scar, not yours' England collapsed in the World Cup semi-final to lose 2-1 to Argentina and Thomas Tuchel has spoken about his in-game tactics for the first time since the tournament ended; Tuchel: "I'm in charge and I take these decisions. No-one is more hurt than me, no-one wanted it more." Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Wednesday 16 September 2026 18:21, UK Image: England could not keep hold of their second-half lead as Argentina reached the World Cup final Thomas Tuchel has passionately defended his controversial defensive substitutions during England's World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina. England were 1-0 up and were five minutes plus stoppage time away from a first World Cup final since 1966. But goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez turned the game on its head, after Tuchel had gone to a back five midway through the second half. Tuchel - who made controversial comments about England's DNA after the semi-final loss - did admit that he may have played a defensive style of play too early in the semi-final. messages.text: WTA reveals new Finals host from 2027 with aim of 'Super Bowl for women's sports'

metadata.summary: The WTA Finals will be staged in Charlotte, North Carolina in the United States from 2027.
metadata.content: WTA Finals: Charlotte's Spectrum Center revealed as new United States home for showpiece WTA event from 2027 season | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content WTA Finals: Charlotte's Spectrum Center revealed as new United States home for showpiece WTA event from 2027 season Women's tour signs three-year deal to take end-of-season event to the North Carolina from 2027; WTA wants to create "Super Bowl for women's sports"; watch the conclusion of the 2026 WTA season live on Sky Sports Tennis, with the Finals at Indian Wells on November 8-15 Wednesday 16 September 2026 16:12, UK Image: 2025's WTA Finals champion Elena Rybakina (right) with runner-up Aryna Sabalenka The WTA Finals will be staged in Charlotte, North Carolina in the United States from 2027. As part of the WTA's desire "to build the preeminent championship experience in women's sport", the tour's showpiece season-ending event for the top eight singles players and doubles teams will be staged at Spectrum Center, the home of the NBA's Charlotte Hornets, in 2027-2029. This year's WTA Finals are taking place in Indian Wells, California in November after the controversial deal to stage the event in Saudi Arabia ended a year early. metadata.summary: The World Grand Prix takes place at Leicester's Mattioli Arena, beginning on September 28, live on Sky Sports.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts 2026: Schedule, format, prize money, venue, dates as Luke Littler, Luke Humphries seek title | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content World Grand Prix Darts 2026: Schedule, format, prize money, venue, dates as Luke Littler, Luke Humphries seek title The draw has been set as Luke Littler looks to defend his World Grand Prix title at Leicester's Mattioli Arena; Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the Boyle Sports World Grand Prix coming up from September 28 to October 4 Wednesday 16 September 2026 13:19, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stephen Bunting says Luke Littler has 'changed' Darts since bursting onto the scene a few years ago, but says he believes 'The Nuke' won't win as many world titles as darts legend Phil Taylor. The World Grand Prix takes place at Leicester's Mattioli Arena, beginning on September 28, live on Sky Sports . The event uniquely requires players to begin and finish every leg on a double or the bullseye. The 32-player field features the top 16 players on the PDC Werner Rankings Ladder and the top 16 players from the ProTour Rankings yet to have qualified, as they bid to claim double-start glory.
